findings.evidence: These two are the only `@[expose]` in TauCeti/Analysis/Semigroups/ (grep); Resolvent.lean:211 uses `T.tendsto_average_orbit_zero` and `expShift_realOperator_apply_of_nonneg`, never the body.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]` from `expShift`; the in-file `rfl` lemmas still elaborate since the body is visible within the module.
findings.issue: `expShift` is `@[expose]`, exposing its body downstream, but its characteristic API is complete (`expShift_apply` simp/rfl, `expShift_apply_apply`, `expShift_realOperator_of_nonneg`, `HasGrowthBound.expShift`) and the only importer (Resolvent.lean) works entirely through those lemmas. No consumer must unfold or compute the body.

findings.evidence: Basic.lean defines `ContractionSemigroup` and `realOperator` without `@[expose]` and exposes only lemmas; same pattern applies here.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]`; the rfl characteristic lemmas remain provable in-file.
findings.issue: `expShiftContraction` is `@[expose]` for no consumer need; its projection (`expShiftContraction_toStronglyContinuousSemigroup`, simp/rfl) and value (`expShiftContraction_apply`, simp) lemmas already characterize it, mirroring the un-exposed `ContractionSemigroup` in Basic.lean.

summary: The characteristic API for both new definitions is complete and correctly annotated, but both `expShift` and `expShiftContraction` are needlessly marked `@[expose]` — the only two in the whole Semigroups directory — even though the full lemma API exists and no consumer unfolds the bodies.
